title: Nasa is looking for new astronauts to send to the moon, and I know who’d be perfect for the job: middle-aged women like me | Helen Pilcher
summary: We’ve been training for this mission for years – solving problems, defusing tensions, keeping everyone fed – and we’d absolutely smash it Nasa is hiring and I’m over the moon. The US space agency is recruiting its next cohort of astronauts to work on the lunar surface and “help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure”. Applications close on 3 December. This isn’t the only job I’ve been swooning over lately. I can’t tell you how many hours I’ve lost to posts about deliciously distant jobs: running the world’s southernmost post office in Antarctica, where staff double as penguin counters, or minding the Great Blasket island off the coast of County Kerry, where the northern lights sometimes shimmer over the North Atlantic. All of it bathed in a warm, rosy glow. In our always-on world, swapping the inbox for an island – or, for the truly frazzled, the moon – seems less like a job and more like a wellness retreat. Helen Pilcher is a science writer and the author of Life Changing: How Humans Are Altering Life on Earth and This Book May Cause Side Effects Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? title: Patients may miss out on NHS weight-loss jabs in England after GP funding withdrawn
summary: Inquiry finds most integrated care boards have scrapped payments to GPs for prescribing and monitoring the drug Patients who are eligible for potentially life-changing weight-loss injections on the NHS risk missing out after most integrated care boards (ICBs) in England withdrew funding for GP services, an investigation has found. The inquiry, conducted by the GP magazine Pulse, found that 21 of 36 ICBs have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring Mounjaro, also known as tirzepatide. A further nine never had a local enhanced service and only four still retain one. Continue reading...

title: Cop31 failed. What happens now? – podcast
summary: The longest ever Cop climate talks have ended in failure after countries were unable to agree a deal. The key sticking point was the omission of any mention of fossil fuels in the final draft. title: Cranberry jam: warming winters and extreme weather threaten a traditional holiday fruit
summary: Scientists are racing to identify and breed new berry varieties that can thrive on an increasingly warmer planet It is harvest time in rural Wisconsin , and the Badger state’s most vibrant crop is painting the rolling countryside a brilliant, unmistakable red. For nearly three decades, Nicole Hansen has been farming cranberries here. Wisconsin produces more than 60% of the nation’s supply. On a crisp fall morning, we waded into a marsh with her to round up the floating harvest.
